r: Demanded amendment of the **1908 Estates Land Act**; paper ***Prajavani*** (ed. **Garimella Krishnamurthy**)
Demanded a **Zamindari Abolition Act**; led the abolition campaign
Presided over by Bharathi Devi Ranga

0.x: **Agriculturists' Debt Relief Bill:** passed by the Madras ministry in **January 1938**.

r: 2nd largest estate of Coastal Andhra; **Palemkota revolt, 20 March 1933**; pullari, kancha paddhati; Gandhi visited **Dec 1933**
Rent taken **in kind instead of cash** → excessive extraction; late 1930s **common lands turned into private lands**
Zamindar **Nayani Venkataranga Rao**; harvest wage cut **80 → 60 seers**; Peasant Association – **Batchala Jagannadh Das**
About 4,000 acres grabbed; leader **Bhupathiraju Lakshmi Narasimha Raju**
**1 April 1940** police firing – 5 killed, incl. Pusumanu Gunnamma
**Ponaka Kanakamma**, Vennelakanti Raghavaiah, Dodla Ramireddy, **Yakasiri Chellamma** (women's chilli-powder resistance)
**Gouthu Latchanna and Pulleti Shyamasundara Rao** carried a petition to the zamindari committee

2.x: Rajaji's Madras ministry appointed a **zamindari committee** chaired by **Revenue Minister T. Prakasam**; report **7 Nov 1938**: **the land belongs to the tiller; the zamindar is only a tax collector**.

r: Bill introduced by Revenue Minister **Kala Venkata Rao**
Passed – **Madras Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act**
**2 April 1949** (called the first law of independent India with the GG's assent)
Abolished zamindari and inam estates; tenants became **direct ryots of the State**; zamindars compensated
Shielded by the **1st (1951)** and **4th (1955)** Amendments; one of the **first abolition laws** of independent India
Occupancy rights for those in possession on **30 June 1934**
About **40%** of Andhra's land; **70%** of the Presidency's zamindari land lay in Andhra districts
